k-1.x_notes: Five pages, every board at actual size with faint triangle grid lines; enough for 40 minutes. Moves from covering shapes with greens (2,3,6,4 — correct) to filling hexagons many ways (chevron does fit, 6 boards plus group count), the hexagram (only blues: forced unique 6-blue tiling, so the 'more than one way?' question has a real answer), big triangles of side 2/3/4 (4, 9, 16; 2x/3x upscale greens fit) and a K-1 entry to kernel 1: blues plus fewest greens on side 2/3/4 triangles (2, 3, 4 greens — a pattern children can notice). Concrete and substantial. Weaknesses: Name field, decorative problem titles, 'Talk about it' and 'Your turn!' boxes that are really adult prompts, exclamation-mark tone ('Cover it all up!'), print notes in place of the organizer's footer, Problem 1 is mostly counting.
k-1.y_notes: Two pages, three numbered problems: fill a rhombus outline with a blue then two greens, a trapezoid with a red then without red, and a 7-triangle 'pennant' filled two ways. Outlines are actual size and correct, and the trade/equal-area idea is sound, but each task takes a minute or two, so the group will be done in about 10-15 minutes — exactly the 'too dumbed down, ends too early' complaint. No contact with either kernel. Format problems: Name/Date, page titles above problems ('The block exchange shop'), 'An adult can read these prompts aloud', 'Build first' line, adult print instructions on the student page, unnumbered 'Play shop'/'Tell or show' sections. Footer matches the organizer's format.
k-1.reason: X gives K-1 children five concrete, well-sized boards that build toward a real idea (fewest greens grows with the triangle), while Y's two thin pages would run out within minutes and never reach the session's mathematics.

grades-2-3.x_notes: Follows kernel 1 closely and correctly. P1: dot the up-triangles on a 4x3 board and record how many ups/downs each block covers (green and red give two answers, blue always 1+1). P2: four even-area boards — A (side-2 triangle, 3 up/1 down) and C (inverted trapezoid, 3 up/5 down) are impossible, B (2-1-1 hexagon) and D (hexagram) are possible; checked. P3: two side-2 hexagons each with 22 white triangles — X removes two ups (impossible), Y removes one up and one down and I verified it tiles. P4-5: fewest greens on side 3/4/5 triangles (3,4,5) with a table to predict side 6 and 10, plus the chevron question. Boards at actual size and fit the page. Real mathematical development from coloring to obstruction to optimal bound. Weaknesses: Name field, titled problems, sub-numbered steps, 'Talk about it'/'Make your own'/'Purple puzzle' boxes, and hints that give the thinking away ('Hint: each blue covers one up and one down', 'leaves only as many gaps as the side length', 'Are they up or down?'). All can be cut in 15 minutes.
grades-2-3.y_notes: Three problems on two outlines (pennant, double hexagon) under an invented 'color rule': copies A and B may not share block colors. Every task is solved almost at once (e.g., two yellows vs four reds; reds vs blues without yellow), so there is little to explore for 40 minutes, and none of kernel 1 (up/down coloring, impossible boards, fewest gaps) appears. Pieces' color is an arbitrary constraint, not the coloring argument. Format problems: Name/Date, cutesy page titles ('Yellow takes a break'), internal labels ('The pennant / P1'), repeated rule boxes on every page, 'Build first', 'Keep exploring', 'Partner puzzle', 'If you want another puzzle', adult print notes. Outlines are actual size; footer is correct.
grades-2-3.reason: X is a correct, well-sequenced investigation of the coloring obstruction and fewest-gap packings with large working boards; Y's color-rule puzzles are trivial, off-kernel, and would leave the four third graders idle.

grades-4-5.x_notes: Delivers kernel 2 fully and correctly. Unit hexagon (exactly 2 tilings, the flip, 3D view); the 1x2x2 'tall hexagon' with 8 blues and 6 tilings (8 recording boxes, so the count is not given away); flip map, fewest flips between the pictured X (ribbon LLRR) and Y (RRLL) = 4; odd round trips; ribbons with a correct worked example (L R R L), words with two L and two R giving 6 tilings, a flip swapping an adjacent LR pair, and an L-score parity argument (each flip changes it by 1) for why round trips are even. Ends with the side-2 hexagon: 12 blues, two ribbons (example L R L R / R L R L is consistent), compatible pairs = comparable pairs in the flip map, 20 tilings. Boards at actual size. Very substantial; more than enough for three children. Weaknesses: Name field, problem titles, a 'Coming up ... secret code' teaser and 'secret code' title, a 'Tips' box with roles and a flip hint, many small numbered sub-steps, and the L-score device printed on the page rather than kept with adults.
grades-4-5.y_notes: Same pennant and double-hexagon outlines as grades 2-3, now minimizing total pieces under the no-shared-colors rule. The mathematics is correct and has a genuine lower-bound flavor (pennant minimum 5 = yellow+green and red+2 blues; double hexagon 6 = 2 yellows + 4 reds; without yellow 10 = 4 reds + 6 blues), and 'why can no smaller total work?' is a good question. But it ignores kernel 2 entirely, the answers fall out quickly for 4th/5th graders, and three problems on two shapes will not fill 40 minutes. 'Think about' lines give the key step away ('If one copy uses yellow, what is the largest block the other can use?'). Same format problems: Name/Date, page titles, P1/P2 labels, 'Build first', adult print notes.
grades-4-5.reason: X is a correct, rich progression through tilings, flips, ribbons and a parity proof with real boards; Y offers a small optimization puzzle unrelated to the outline that the older children would finish early.

overall.reason: In every band X carries the outline's mathematics with correct, well-sized boards and enough substantial work for the full forty minutes; its faults (Name fields, titles, talk boxes, giveaway hints, a cutesy teaser) are deletions that fit in a 15-minute edit. Y is thin in all three bands, swaps the kernels for an arbitrary color rule, and would need to be rewritten rather than edited.
